definition: A model overlay is a manual adjustment applied to a model's output by someone outside the model itself, used to impose a firm's own judgment on top of the model's calculation.
core_idea: Firm management can override or scale a model's output from the outside — for example, deliberately doubling a worst-case loss estimate to be more conservative — without changing the model's internal logic.
key_points: The overlay comes from an external source (e.g., firm management), not from the model's own calculation.
The example given is management doubling the risk team's worst-case loss estimate to get a more conservative figure.
It is presented as a discrete tool distinct from both position limits and modeling reserves.
relationships: One of the named tools/terms under model risk controls, alongside modeling reserve.
trading_implications: Risk figures reported to a firm's leadership may already reflect a deliberate conservative adjustment layered on top of the raw model output, not the model's unadjusted number.
